items.title: Multi server network core
items.summary: Four servers behind one address, sharing permissions, chat and player data.
items.description: Built for a network that had outgrown a single Paper instance. Each gamemode runs on its own server, so a crash on minigames never touches survival, and LuckPerms contexts keep one permission tree across all of them.
highlights: Held 12ms average tick time with 400 players on
Rolling restarts, so nobody gets kicked for a server cycle

items.title: Permission tree rebuild
items.summary: Ninety tangled permission groups cut down to fourteen inherited tracks in one weekend.
items.description: The old setup granted permissions per user with no inheritance at all, so every promotion meant hand editing about forty nodes. After the rebuild a rank change is one command.
highlights: Promotions went from 40 manual edits to a single command
Every track documented in the staff handbook

items.title: Discord community structure
items.summary: A 40 channel layout with staged access that took a community from 400 to 12,000 members.
items.description: New members land in six channels. The rest opens up as they verify, introduce themselves and actually take part, which keeps the first impression readable instead of overwhelming.
highlights: Verified onboarding took spam joins down to almost nothing

items.title: Closed loop server economy
items.summary: Shops, jobs and a player market balanced so money actually leaves the economy again.
items.description: Server economies usually inflate because currency comes in faster than it goes out. This one pairs every income source with a sink, and I modelled the numbers before anything went live.
highlights: Currency supply stayed flat across a full 90 day season

items.title: Moderation and staff systems
items.summary: Hiring rubrics, shift rotas and an escalation ladder for an eleven person team spread across three timezones.
items.description: The technical side was the easy part. The real work was writing decision rules clear enough that a new moderator on their first shift knows what to do without pinging an owner at 3am.
highlights: Turnover fell to two people leaving in nine months
Every type of decision has a named owner

items.title: Custom quest and content chain
items.summary: Sixty custom items and a matching encounter chain that carried an SMP through its first season.
items.description: Items, mobs and quests were configured together rather than separately, so every reward has a use and every encounter exists for a reason beyond filling out a menu.
highlights: 38% of players were still around at day 30

items.title: Verification and ticket automation
items.summary: One verification, ticket and logging stack, deployed across eleven communities.
items.description: Built once, parameterised, then rolled out to eleven servers with different rules. Each owner got documentation so they could change it later without touching a bot dashboard.
highlights: Eleven communities running off one documented template

items.title: Performance and stability pass
items.summary: A plugin audit and tuning job that took average tick time from 41ms to 12ms.
items.description: Nine plugins removed, four replaced, chunk loading and entity limits retuned. No hardware upgrade needed, because the hardware was never the problem.
